items.followUp: Define a function declaration in C.

rubric.why: A prototype is identified as a declaration of a function.
rubric.description: Identifies a prototype as a function declaration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a prototype declares a function.

rubric.why: These are the details that a prototype specifies before the function is defined.
rubric.description: States the details given in a function prototype.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the function’s return type and parameters, or explaining that it is declared before its definition.

modelAnswer: A function prototype is a declaration that tells the compiler a function’s name, return type and parameters before the function is defined.

rubric.why: Each hexadecimal digit is converted to its equivalent four-bit binary group.
rubric.description: Correctly converts the hexadecimal digits to four-bit groups.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing A = 1010, 2 = 0010 and 3 = 0011.

rubric.why: The groups combine to give the correct binary number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final binary answer.

items.followUp: How does volatile memory differ from non-volatile memory?

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory retains its contents when power is removed.
rubric.description: States that stored data is retained without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that data remains when the computer is switched off.

rubric.why: This describes the outcome of non-volatile memory retaining information.
rubric.description: Explains that the data remains stored until changed or erased.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that data is retained until it is changed or erased.

modelAnswer: Non-volatile memory retains its stored data even when the power is switched off.
The data remains stored until it is changed or erased.

items.followUp: State the base and digits used in the octal and binary number systems.

rubric.why: These identify the decimal system’s base and digit set.
rubric.description: States the base or digits of the decimal system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that decimal is base 10 and uses digits 0 to 9.

rubric.why: These identify the binary system’s base and digit set.
rubric.description: States the base or digits of the binary system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that binary is base 2 and uses digits 0 and 1.

modelAnswer: The decimal system has base 10 and uses the digits 0 to 9.
The binary system has base 2 and uses the digits 0 and 1.

items.followUp: Write the truth table for X OR Y.

rubric.why: These are the four possible combinations of truth values for X and Y.
rubric.description: Includes all four combinations of X and Y.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for listing TT, TF, FT and FF.

rubric.why: The conjunction is true only when both propositions are true.
rubric.description: Gives the correct X AND Y result for each row.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for output values T, F, F, F in the corresponding rows.

modelAnswer: For X AND Y, the result is true only when both X and Y are true.

items.followUp: When is the logical AND operator true?

rubric.why: OR is used to combine logical conditions or expressions.
rubric.description: States that OR combines conditions or expressions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that OR joins two or more conditions.

rubric.why: The OR result is true when at least one condition is true and false only when both are false.
rubric.description: Explains the truth condition for OR.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that OR is true if at least one condition is true, and false if both are false.

modelAnswer: The OR operator is used to combine two or more conditions.
It gives a true result if at least one condition is true; it is false only when both conditions are false.

items.followUp: What is a proposition in logic?

rubric.why: A truth value is one of the two possible logical values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming true and false as the possible values.

rubric.why: Truth values are assigned to propositions or logical statements.
rubric.description: Explains what a truth value applies to.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the value assigned to a proposition or logical statement.

modelAnswer: A truth value is the value assigned to a proposition or logical statement.
It is either true or false.

items.followUp: Name any two layers of the OSI network model other than the Application layer.

rubric.why: Each listed term is a layer of the OSI model.
rubric.description: Names one valid OSI model layer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming one OSI layer.

rubric.why: A second valid layer completes the requested pair.
rubric.description: Names a second valid OSI model layer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming another OSI layer.

modelAnswer: Two layers of the OSI network model are the Physical layer and the Network layer.
